use_case_name: Publish Subsurface Surveillance and Acoustic Contact Reports

claims.content: The C2 JU publishes subsurface surveillance and acoustic contact reports by exchanging tactically significant information derived from ASW sensors using J3.0, J3.4, and J5.4 messages to report bearings, ranges, tracks, and datum in accordance with specific reporting criteria and responsibility rules.

goal.raw_text: The C2 JU publishes subsurface surveillance and acoustic contact reports by exchanging tactically significant information derived from ASW sensors using J3.0, J3.4, and J5.4 messages to report bearings, ranges, tracks, and datum in accordance with specific reporting criteria and responsibility rules.

claims.content: C2 JU
The information on the subsurface track must be as complete, accurate, and timely as possible before reporting.

Proper rules for reporting a subsurface track must be followed, including providing source track data (Source TN), reporting established local tracks with all known parameters at the next opportunity, and time-tagging all data.

Reporting responsibility (R²) for a subsurface contact must be established; the first JU to report assumes responsibility unless a Drop Track message is received or no update is received for two consecutive periods.
Subsurface surveillance reports shall include geodetic latitude and longitude in the J3.4 message, and may include depth when available.
Velocity of subsurface tracks shall be reported as course (degrees true north) and speed (data miles per hour ground speed).
Time of contact acquisition, datum establishment, current position, or loss shall be reported in Hour, Minute, and Time Function fields of the J3.4C1 word.
A C2 JU detects or acquires a subsurface contact requiring reporting, or receives acoustic bearing/range data from ASW sensors that must be exchanged as tactically significant information.

trigger.raw_text: A C2 JU detects or acquires a subsurface contact requiring reporting, or receives acoustic bearing/range data from ASW sensors that must be exchanged as tactically significant information.

claims.content: The C2 JU uses J3.0, J3.4, and J5.4 messages to exchange tactically significant information derived from ASW sensors to report bearings, ranges, and tracks.

When reporting a subsurface track, the C2 JU must provide the source of track data (Source TN), report established local tracks with all known parameters at the next opportunity, and ensure all data is time-tagged.

The first JU to report a contact assumes reporting responsibility (R²) for that Track Number; no other JU shall report the contact using that track number unless a Drop Track message is received or no update is received for two consecutive periods.

If the detecting sensor is integral to the reporting JU, the Origin TN field in the J5.4 message shall contain the TN of the reporting JU; if integral to another unit, it shall contain the TN of the detecting unit.
When contact is lost, the C2 JU may report the track as a DATUM in a J3.4 message with Data Report Type (DRT) = 4, including the last known position and time contact was lost.
If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received containing the Track Number, another JU may report the contact using that Track Number.
If a J3.4 message containing the Track Number is not received for two consecutive periodic updates, another JU may assume reporting responsibility and report the contact using that Track Number.
Any other JU may report what it believes to be the same subsurface contact using a different Track Number, but shall only include locally derived data in the J3.4 message.

When contact is lost, the decision to report a DATUM is an operator function, and the DATUM is reported in a J3.4 message with Data Report Type (DRT) = 4, using the same Reference TN as the lost track.
In the DATUM report, the ASW Time Function is set to 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), and Hour/Minute fields contain the truncated time contact was lost or DATUM established.
The DATUM report includes latitude, longitude, 15 meters depth, and depth contact fields set to the last known position of the contact.
Although last known course and speed are reported in the DATUM, the DATUM itself shall not move; these values are used only for DATUM Error calculation and ASW search planning.
If contact is regained, a J3.4 message with DRT set to 0, 1, or 2 shall be reported with the same TN as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action.
A DATUM shall only be dropped or purged by explicit operator action.

When a JU determines a Subsurface Interface Unit (IU) is no longer active and holds local data on it, the JU assumes reporting responsibility by reporting a J3.4 Subsurface Track message using the inactive IU address as the reference TN.
If the inactive IU returns to active status, the JU holding reporting responsibility shall cease reporting the IU, but shall not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.
If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received containing the Track Number, another JU may report the contact using that Track Number.
If a J3.4 message containing the Track Number is not received for two consecutive periodic updates, another JU may assume reporting responsibility and report the contact using that Track Number.

When contact is lost, the decision to report a DATUM is an operator function; if chosen, it is reported in a J3.4 message with Data Report Type (DRT) = 4, using the same Reference TN as the lost track.
In the DATUM report, the ASW Time Function is set to 3 (Time Contact Lost) or 1 (Time Datum Established), and Hour/Minute fields contain the truncated time contact was lost or DATUM established.

The DATUM report includes latitude, longitude, 15 meters depth, and depth contact fields set to the last known position of the contact; although last known course and speed are reported, the DATUM itself shall not move.
A DATUM shall only be dropped or purged by explicit operator action.
If contact is regained, a J3.4 message with DRT set to 0, 1, or 2 shall be reported with the same TN as the DATUM, or a new TN depending on operator action.
The information on the subsurface track is as complete, accurate, and timely as possible.

Proper rules for reporting a subsurface track have been followed, including providing source track data (Source TN), reporting established local tracks with all known parameters at the next opportunity, and time-tagging all data.

Reporting responsibility (R²) for the subsurface contact has been established; the first JU to report assumes responsibility unless a Drop Track message is received or no update is received for two consecutive periods.
Subsurface surveillance reports include geodetic latitude and longitude in the J3.4 message, and may include depth when available.
Velocity of subsurface tracks has been reported as course (degrees true north) and speed (data miles per hour ground speed).
Time of contact acquisition, datum establishment, current position, or loss has been reported in Hour, Minute, and Time Function fields of the J3.4C1 word.
If contact was lost, the C2 JU has the capability to report the track as a DATUM in a J3.4 message with Data Report Type (DRT) = 4, including last known position and time contact was lost.
